info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "veo/veo-3.0-generate-001", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: This model's input has not been narrowed by Comfy yet. Router forwards the body to the partner unchanged, so the partner's own documentation is authoritative until a schema is authored for this model. Any JSON object is accepted here and by the server's pre-provider validation alike.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Veo models: the terminal Vertex AI long-running operation document, forwarded unchanged. Veo is submit-and-poll, and Router polls on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is the finished operation (`done: true`) rather than the operation handle the submit returns.
The generated videos are in `response.videos`. Each carries either `gcsUri` or `bytesBase64Encoded` (the video inline), and `mimeType` names the container. `response.raiMediaFilteredCount` and `response.raiMediaFilteredReasons` report videos Vertex's responsible-AI filters removed, so a `done: true` operation can legitimately carry fewer videos than were requested — or none at all.
WHICH OF THE TWO YOU GET depends on the environment, and `gcsUri` is the one field Router does not forward unchanged. TREAT BOTH MEMBERS AS POSSIBLE AND READ WHICHEVER IS PRESENT. Where platform storage is enabled for `veo/*`, Router asks Vertex to write the clips to Cloud Storage rather than inline them and then replaces each `gcsUri` it owns with a SIGNED HTTPS URL you can fetch directly, valid for 24 hours; everything else in the document is Vertex's own. Where it is not enabled, Vertex inlines the clips as `bytesBase64Encoded` and the whole document is forwarded unchanged. Two further cases are always answered with the partner's own value: a request that sets `parameters.storageUri` to a bucket of its own keeps that bucket and its `gs://` URIs, untouched, and a bring-your-own-key call runs entirely in your project and is likewise left alone.
The example's `gcsUri` is a placeholder, with the signature query the real answer carries deliberately omitted: a signed URL published in a spec is a leaked credential and a dead link at once.
ONE MEMBER IS AUTHORED AHEAD OF ENABLEMENT. `veo/veo-2.0-generate-001` resolves to the literal `POST /proxy/veo/generate` operation rather than the collapsed `/:modelId/generate` one, and `routerresult/classification.go` records a return mode only for the latter — so `runRouterModel` refuses it before dispatch until that row lands. The other five members are classified and run today.

response.description: The prediction response, present when done is true

raiMediaFilteredCount.description: Number of videos filtered by responsible AI policies

raiMediaFilteredReasons.description: Reasons why videos were filtered by responsible AI policies

gcsUri.description: Cloud Storage URI of the generated video
